newsitem.title: USA: World Bank to lend Macedonia $60 million.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to lend Macedonia $60 million.

text.p: The World Bank said on Tuesday it approved a total of $60 million in loans for the former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia in support of the government's economic reform programme.
The loans are aimed at spurring economic growth by promoting reforms in the trade and agricultural sectors and by fostering private sector development.

"Significant economic distortions in the trade and agricultural sectors continue to constrain the efficiency of the private sector, thereby undermining overall economic recover," the World Bank said in a statement.
The planned reforms include further trade liberalisation and privatisation.
The Bank said that $30 million will be provided by its International Development Association affiliate, which lends money at virtually no cost to the world's poorest nations.
The remaining $30 million will be lent in German marks at market-related interest rates for 20-year credits.
